To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the antileishmania activity of the dehydroabietyl derivatives is mainly dependent on the substitution pattern of the aromatic ring, the presence of the amide group and the lipophilicity of the molecule.
the dehydroabietyl derivatives 8 and 15 showed promising antileishmaniasis activity.
a series of dehydroabietylaminobenzamide derivatives were found to be active against promastigotes and intracellular amastogtes of Leishmania species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a new series of dehydroabietyl amide derivatives and their evaluation as antileishmanials.
the development of new antiparasitic drugs, and the results herein presented show the potential of the abietane-type diperpenoids for the treatment of leishmaniasis.
the synthesis of new derivatives with promising antileishmaniasis activity, which may be further explored for the development of new antiprotozoals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the C7- and/or C12-functionalized derivatives are more active than (+)-dehydroabietic acid and (+)-dehydro-abietylamine, which is in agreement with the results obtained in other studies with abietane-type compounds.
these compounds, especially the acetamide 15, may be considered as potential candidates for the development of new antileishmaniasis drugs.
the presence of a 3,5-di-tert-butylbenzamide group at C7 of dehydroabietylaminyl derivatives is essential to improve the antileishmania activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of a benzyl group in the C7 position of dehydroabietyl derivatives, in addition to an aromatic moiety at C12, seems to be the best structural arrangement for the antileshmanial activity of these diterpenoids.
the antileishmania activity was not directly correlated with the lipophilicity, but with the presence of a polar group in the C12-position.
compounds 8 and/or 10, which are benzamide derivatives, are the best lead compounds for the development of a new antileishmaniasis drug.
The main takeaway from our work is that
C12-alkylated benzamides are the most active derivatives, and C7-alkylated compounds are inactive.
these derivatives are potential candidates for further antileishmaniasis drug development.
C7 and C12 functionalized dehydroabietylamines are a promising scaffold for the development of antileishmanials.
